newsitem.title: UK: UK's IoD urges government to cut red tape.
newsitem.headline: UK's IoD urges government to cut red tape.

text.p: British business regulation costs firms 43 billion pounds per year and the government should target key areas like tax administration to help cut costs, the Institute of Directors (IoD) said on Tuesday.
It said around 8,000 new rules had been introduced since the government began its deregulation drive in 1993, generating an extra bill to British business of around 8.4 billion stg.
The IoD, a leading business lobby, has launched a deregulation "hit list' to help focus the government on key areas where businesses are hardest hit, such as health and safety and employment law.
"It is clear current regulations are over-burdensome on business. Effective deregulation must be made a top priority for government," said IoD business economist Alison Cansfield.

Among the recommendations was to establish an effective system of accounting for new regulations and to publish details in a monthly regulatory report. The IoD also recommended a "forms and statistics' budget to limit the number of surveys government departments can send out to small businesses.
